title: 2026 so far
tagline: Chatbots in half of pockets, driverless taxis in a dozen cities and a crew around the Moon: the year to 18 October.

locale.persona: a hybrid-working household in a mid-sized Midwestern city

sceneCaption: A pair of smart glasses on a charging stand beside an open earbuds case.

morningRoutine.detail: About 22.6 percent of U.S. workers teleworked or worked at home for pay in March 2026, so many households still plan the morning around who is going in.

source.label: BLS TED: 22.6 percent of workers teleworked in March 2026

morningRoutine.detail: About half of U.S. adults (49 percent) said in February 2026 that they use AI chatbots, up from about a third in 2024; the questions were not asked in quite the same way.

source.label: Pew Research Center: About half of U.S. adults now use AI chatbots, up from a third in 2024 (11 June 2026)

morningRoutine.detail: Eggs cost about $2.27 a dozen in September 2026, well below the $3.49 of a year earlier.

source.label: BLS: Average retail food and energy prices, U.S. city average (September 2026)

morningRoutine.detail: Regular gasoline averaged about $4.48 a gallon in September 2026, up from $4.20 in August.

source.label: BLS via FRED: Gasoline, Unleaded Regular, per gallon (APU000074714)

places.title: The front page
places.description: A year of spaceflight, a home World Cup and the nation's 250th birthday.
places.imageAlt: A news app showing the Moon flyby and the World Cup final
highlights: Artemis II flies four astronauts around the Moon (1 to 10 April)
Spain beats Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final (19 July)
The country marks 250 years since the Declaration of Independence (4 July)
Midterm elections are scheduled for 3 November

source.label: Wikipedia: 2026 in the United States

places.title: The bedside
places.description: The phone is where the day begins, and more and more of what people do on it is a conversation with a chatbot.
places.imageAlt: A phone on a bedside table beside a pair of smart glasses on a charging stand
highlights: About half of U.S. adults use AI chatbots (Pew, February 2026)
Up from about a third in 2024

source.label: Pew Research Center: About half of U.S. adults now use AI chatbots, up from a third in 2024 (11 June 2026)

places.title: The street
places.description: In a growing list of cities a car with no driver pulls up to the kerb.
places.imageAlt: A driverless taxi at a city kerb
highlights: Waymo carried about 500,000 paid rides a week by June 2026
Full service began in Miami (15 April), Nashville (25 June), Dallas (4 August) and Houston (20 August)

technology.name: AI chatbots
technology.description: About half of U.S. adults (49 percent) used AI chatbots in Pew's February 2026 survey, up from about a third in 2024.

source.label: Pew Research Center: About half of U.S. adults now use AI chatbots, up from a third in 2024 (11 June 2026)

technology.name: Driverless taxis
technology.description: Waymo reported about 500,000 paid rides a week and nearly 3,900 robotaxis in service by June 2026, with full service in cities from Phoenix to Houston.

source.label: Wikipedia: Waymo

technology.name: Smart glasses
technology.description: Glasses with cameras, microphones and small displays went on general sale: Meta Ray-Ban Display in September 2025 and Meta's own glasses at $299 in June 2026, with Google's eyewear promised for the fall.

source.label: Wikipedia: Smartglasses

technology.name: Electric cars
technology.description: About 262,000 electric vehicles were sold in the third quarter of 2026, roughly 6.4 percent of new-vehicle sales, up from 5.8 percent in the second quarter.

source.label: Cox Automotive: Q3 2026 EV sales (12 October 2026)

technology.name: Phone-to-satellite service
technology.description: SpaceX renamed its direct-to-phone satellite service Starlink Mobile in March 2026; ordinary LTE phones connect directly to satellites for texting where cell coverage is missing.

source.label: Wikipedia: Starlink

futureVisions.prediction: Powerful AI, smarter than a Nobel Prize winner across most relevant fields, could come as early as 2026, though it could take much longer.
futureVisions.whoSaidIt: Dario Amodei, essay 'Machines of Loving Grace', October 2024
futureVisions.note: Too early to judge: this year is not over.

source.label: Dario Amodei: Machines of Loving Grace (October 2024)

futureVisions.prediction: 2026 will likely see the arrival of systems that can figure out novel insights.
futureVisions.whoSaidIt: Sam Altman, blog post 'The Gentle Singularity' (undated on the page)
